clue.text: Even agitato passage may be so written!

definitions.text: Even agitato passage may be so written!

parts.words: Even agitato passage may be so written!
parts.note: a piece of music is set down by its writer, and the word for that also means calm, the opposite of agitated

explanation.surface: A remark that even a frantic stretch of music has to be calmly set down on paper.
explanation.walkthrough: The joke is the two senses: a written-out piece of music, and a calm state, which an agitato passage pointedly is not.
explanation.definitionFit: A piece of music is described as having been written by its maker, while the same word means calm and collected.

clue.text: Antiquated, so allowed to be held in honour

indicators.note: the honour's letters hold the other pieces within them

parts.note: OBE, Order of the British Empire, is a British honour
taken as written
let means allowed

explanation.surface: Something old-fashioned, permitted to remain among the honours.
explanation.walkthrough: An OBE (Officer of the Order of the British Empire) is a British royal honour, so 'honour' gives letters here, not an abstract virtue.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe something out of date and no longer in use.

clue.text: Transport for a small charge

parts.note: a small charge here is a little one in someone's care, a baby, rather than a low fee

explanation.surface: Cheap travel at a low fare.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Charge' looks like a price, but it is a person in one's care; a small one is a baby, whose transport is a pram.
explanation.definitionFit: A baby carriage is a pushed vehicle for an infant, the formal British name for a pram.

clue.text: Angry about doctor, and not happy

indicators.note: the word for angry goes around the doctor's letters

parts.note: sore can mean angry or aggrieved
MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a doctor's qualification

explanation.surface: Someone cross with their doctor and in a gloomy mood.
explanation.definitionFit: Gloomy and dismal in mood is the opposite of cheerful.

clue.text: Exploit that should be witnessed

definitions.meaning: a legal document that must be signed in front of a witness

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a notable act and a signed legal document requiring a witness's signature.

clue.text: Teams in the markets for more than left-wingers

indicators.note: the teams are placed inside the markets

parts.note: marts are markets
XI (eleven) is a cricket or football team, so XIS are teams

explanation.surface: Sports sides at the markets competing for something beyond the political left.
explanation.walkthrough: A team of eleven is written XI, the Roman numeral; the definition says these are further left than mere left-wingers.
explanation.definitionFit: Followers of Karl Marx's communism are thought of as extreme socialists, beyond ordinary leftists.

clue.text: Return of service takes love game

indicators.note: return means the service's letters are read the other way

parts.note: the RAF (Royal Air Force) is one of the armed services
love is zero in tennis, shaped like the letter O

explanation.surface: A tennis rally: the serve comes back and wins a love game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Return', 'service', 'love' and 'game' all suggest tennis; RAF read backwards gives FAR.
explanation.definitionFit: Faro is an old gambling card game in which players bet on the order of cards.

clue.text: This class is certain to be kept in idle fashion

indicators.note: the word for certain is held inside the reworked letters
to fashion something is to shape it anew, so the letters of idle are rearranged

parts.note: sure means certain

explanation.surface: A class of people sure to be kept idle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fashion' rearranges the letters of 'idle', and 'to be kept in' puts the word for certain inside them. The definition calls the answer 'this class': the idle rich.
explanation.definitionFit: Those with plenty of free time and no need to work are called the leisured class.

clue.text: It's clear the girl has a cute wiggle

parts.note: Eva is a girl's name

indicators.note: a wiggle moves things about, so the letters of a cute are rearranged

explanation.surface: A girl with a cute wriggle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wiggle' rearranges the letters of 'a cute', which follow the girl's name; 'It's' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To empty a building of people is to clear it out.

clue.text: Holy man turns to a king and emperor

indicators.note: turns means the holy man's letters face the other way

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for saint
R, from Latin rex, means king

explanation.surface: A saint turns to a king and an emperor.
explanation.walkthrough: ST read backwards gives TS.
explanation.definitionFit: The Russian ruler's title came from Caesar, an imperial title.

clue.text: With right on both sides?

parts.note: having a right hand on each side, figuratively able to use either hand equally

explanation.surface: Someone who is in the right whichever side of an argument they take.
explanation.walkthrough: 'right' seems to mean justified, but think of the right hand: someone who has two of them can use either hand.
explanation.definitionFit: Being equally skilful with both hands is like having two right hands.

clue.text: Snacks for new students in rest break

indicators.note: the new students go inside the other letters
breaking the word rest scatters its letters into a new order

parts.note: freshmen are first-year students

explanation.surface: Food for freshers during a rest break.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rest break' looks like a pause; 'break' instead rearranges the letters of 'rest' to RETS, and 'in' puts the new students between its two halves.
explanation.definitionFit: Light food and drink served at an event are called this.

clue.text: Injury received in turning over?

parts.note: reads as a fracture from a fall, but in cricket an over is six balls, and a ball that spins from the leg side is so called

explanation.surface: A broken limb picked up while falling over.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a bowler delivers an 'over' of six balls; a leg break is a delivery spun from leg to off. The surface reads it as a fractured leg.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket this is a slow ball that spins from the leg side; literally it is a fractured limb.

clue.text: A card cheat may be so described

definitions.text: A card cheat may be so described

parts.words: A card cheat may be so described
parts.note: a playing card, the jack, and a dishonest rogue share one name

explanation.surface: A remark on how to describe someone who cheats at cards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'card cheat' seems one person, but it is two senses: a card (the jack) and a cheat (a rogue).
explanation.definitionFit: The jack in a pack of cards has an old name that also means a dishonest rascal.

clue.text: Bear — with a sore head possibly?

definitions.text: Bear — with a sore head possibly?

parts.words: Bear — with a sore head possibly?
parts.note: bear as a verb means to endure pain, as one would with a headache, playing on the idiom of a bear with a sore head

explanation.surface: A grumpy bear, as in the British idiom 'like a bear with a sore head'.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Like a bear with a sore head' is a British idiom for being very grumpy; here 'bear' is the verb, to endure, as one does a headache.
explanation.definitionFit: To bear pain is to endure or undergo it, as with a sore head.

clue.text: Group of agents in prison

definitions.meaning: a small unit of spies or activists working together
a small room where a prisoner is locked up

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a small secret unit of operatives and a lock-up room in a jail.

clue.text: Two birds seen at daybreak

parts.note: a cock is a male bird
a crow is a black bird

explanation.surface: A pair of birds spotted at dawn.
explanation.definitionFit: Dawn is traditionally marked by a rooster's call.

clue.text: Cut back writing in papers

indicators.note: back means the word for cut is read in reverse

parts.note: to axe something is to cut it
MS is the abbreviation for manuscript, a piece of writing

explanation.surface: Reduced writing in the newspapers.
explanation.walkthrough: AXE read backwards gives EXA; 'papers' are question papers, not newspapers.
explanation.definitionFit: Exam papers are the written tests taken by students.

clue.text: Weather men caught in a flurry of sleet

indicators.note: the men are trapped inside the rearranged letters
a flurry is a swirl, so the letters of sleet are blown about

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Weathermen caught out by a sudden shower of sleet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Weather men' reads as forecasters, but 'Weather' alone is the definition. 'a flurry of' rearranges the letters of 'sleet' to ELETS, and 'caught in' places the men inside.
explanation.definitionFit: The elements are wind, rain and other forces of the weather.

clue.text: She will be about to have a meal

indicators.note: about here means turned round, so the meal word is read backwards

parts.note: to dine is to have a meal

explanation.surface: A woman who is just about to eat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about to' looks like a phrase meaning soon; 'about' is the reversal signal, turning DINE round.
explanation.definitionFit: Enid is a woman's name, so it can stand for a female person.

clue.text: I mention novel straightaway

indicators.note: novel means new, so the letters of I mention take a new order

explanation.surface: Someone mentions a novel immediately.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means very quickly, at once.

clue.text: Keep in one piece

definitions.meaning: a keep is a fortified tower or stronghold
a chess piece, also called a rook

explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a fortified building and the chessman called a rook.

clue.text: The plane might be a jumbo

indicators.note: might be suggests the letters of the plane could become something else when rearranged

explanation.surface: A remark that the aircraft could be a jumbo jet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jumbo' looks like a Boeing 747, but the word is a name for a large pachyderm.
explanation.definitionFit: Jumbo, a famous circus animal, gave his name to anything huge, including the large tusked beast.

clue.text: Sallies follow a direction to arms

indicators.note: follow means the sallies come after the direction

parts.note: E is east, a compass direction
sallies are witty remarks, quips

explanation.surface: Sorties follow orders to take up arms.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sallies' suggests military sorties, but here they are witty remarks.
explanation.definitionFit: To arm someone is to supply them with gear or weapons.

clue.text: School teacher upset about hours being changed

indicators.note: the letters of teacher and hours are altered into a new order

explanation.surface: A teacher is upset about the timetable being altered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being changed' rearranges TEACHER and HOURS together; 'upset about' is part of the surface. Charterhouse is an English private school.
explanation.definitionFit: Charterhouse is a well-known English independent school in Surrey.

clue.text: Sailor boy in his hammock

parts.note: AB, able seaman, is a sailor
Ed is a boy's name

explanation.surface: A young sailor resting in his hammock.
explanation.definitionFit: Lying in a hammock means being in bed.

clue.text: Being deceived outright is tough

annotationWithheld.why: Being deceived outright is tough: HA(R)D needs 'outright' as both the container signal 'out' and the letter R for 'right', one word doing two jobs

clue.text: A hard thing to catch

definitions.meaning: a horny tip on a finger or a metal spike

explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a hard fingertip covering or metal spike and a verb meaning to apprehend.

clue.text: Musical show high-spot for a worker

parts.note: an opera is a musical stage work
a tor is a rocky hill, a high spot

explanation.surface: A musical highlight for a worker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'high-spot' looks like a highlight; it is a tor, a rocky hilltop in southwest England.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who runs a machine or business is a worker of a kind.

clue.text: Is backing on to the street, but caught in the act and stopped

indicators.note: the other pieces are trapped inside the act's letters

parts.note: a deed is an act

indicators.note: backing means the word is is reversed

explanation.surface: A burglar backing on to the street, caught in the act and halted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' turns 'Is' round to SI, and 'caught in' puts that and the street inside the act; 'but' and 'on to' are only links.
explanation.definitionFit: To leave off doing something is to cease.
